newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai's gold imports dip in August - WGC.
newsitem.headline: Dubai's gold imports dip in August - WGC.

text.p: Gold imports into the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai fell 1.04 tonnes to 28.848 tonnes in August, the World Gold Council in Dubai reported on Sunday.
The figures coincide with a seasonal downturn in trade because of the harsh Gulf summer which caps business as expatriates and Gulf nationals remain away on vacation.
Switzerland remained the main gold supplier to Dubai at 21.378 tonnes down from 22.331 in July, followed by Britain at 6.264 tonnes down from 6.451 tonnes.
Total bullion imports into Dubai totalled 228 tonnes between January and August, up from 219 tonnes in the same period last year.
Approximately 80 percent of Dubai's gold imports are re-exported to the Indian sub-continent, mostly to India which is the world's single largest gold consumer.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by traders at 5,267 UAE dirhmams ($1,435.15), down 18 dirhams on the week.
"Shipments to India are going very well. Demand is not depressed there," a regular supplier to India said.
